purpose: settle #1473: attribute the g500-ladder rung-level peak RSS figure
method: One delegated systemd user scope per ladder attempt under a shared benchexec slice; 200 ms cgroup-v2 sampling of hierarchical memory.stat, memory.peak, per-child cgroup memory facts, and summed descendant /proc VmHWM, alongside the rung's own certify VmHWM phase authority and BenchExec resource authority. Two complete passed S18 rungs on the same source, binaries, host, and work root.
verdict: The rung-level peak figure is cgroup memory usage, not resident process memory: at the tool scope's peak, file (page cache) is 74.6% and anon 21.9%. The cgroup peak tracks bytes moved; certify's per-phase VmHWM stays 3.2x below it and measures the anonymous working set the 4 GiB envelope governs. The two figures disagree by construction, not by defect; since the #1278 repair the admission gate consumes the process VmHWM authority.
limitations: Point-in-time observations on one host; the launcher scope's own page cache is excluded from tool-scope figures by cgroup separation; sampler resolution is 200 ms while memory.peak is kernel-authoritative.
